items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He and Fred Ramsey... they wrote a book called Jazzmen... I read that pretty much as it came out.

ctx.x: Let’s start to talk about these writers and people whose footsteps you followed in. You mentioned Charles Edward Smith. I’d like to talk about George Frazier and Roger Pryor Dodge and people like that. Let’s start with Smith. What’s his place from two perspectives: (a) you, the young 20-year-old, in 1945?; and (b) from our perspective today? Where do you see Charles Edward Smith?

I wish people read him now. I don’t think it’s a name that would mean much, even to some of the people – younger people who write about the music. He and Fred Ramsey, who was also a very good writer and researcher and traveler, they wrote a book called Jazzmen, I think. I read that pretty much as it came out. That was like reading a romance. They made not only the musicians come alive – obviously they talked to various – a lot of people – but you got the whole ambience, the sense of what New Orleans was like and…
